steps.intent: Algeria's primary objective is to mandate an immediate humanitarian ceasefire to halt the ongoing massacre in Gaza, avert an impending catastrophe in Rafah, and prevent any forced displacement of Palestinians. We also seek to embed the International Court of Justice's provisional measures and enforce unhindered humanitarian access at scale. The principal point of contention is the explicit demand for an immediate ceasefire, which the United States opposes on the grounds that it could undermine ongoing hostage and truce negotiations in Doha and Cairo, making a US veto the primary obstacle despite overwhelming Council support.

messages.China: China fully supports the draft resolution submitted by Algeria on behalf of the Arab Group. An immediate humanitarian ceasefire is the overriding prerequisite to save civilian lives and halt an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe, especially in light of the looming military offensive against Rafah. We call on all Council members to heed the overwhelming call of the international community and support the swift adoption of this text without delay.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador thanks Algeria for presenting this draft resolution at a critical juncture, as the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza worsens and the threat of an offensive in Rafah looms. We fully support an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, and full compliance with international humanitarian law. To foster greater unity within the Council and ensure a balanced text, we believe it is essential to include explicit condemnation of the terrorist attacks of 7 October.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft's call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the urgent surge of humanitarian relief to prevent famine, and the explicit rejection of a ground offensive in Rafah. However, the Council must not remain silent on the worst terrorist attack in Israel's history; we strongly urge the penholder to incorporate an unequivocal condemnation of Hamas and the 7 October attacks. We are committed to working constructively to secure a strong, balanced resolution that meets the humanitarian emergency while upholding international law and the fight against terrorism.
messages.Guyana: Guyana commends Algeria for presenting this timely and critically needed draft resolution and expresses its full support for the text as drafted. An immediate humanitarian ceasefire is urgently required to avert an even greater catastrophe in Gaza, particularly in light of the dire conditions facing civilians in Rafah. We also welcome the strong reaffirmation of international humanitarian law, the call for the unconditional release of all hostages, and the explicit reference to the International Court of Justice's provisional measures.
messages.Japan: Japan shares the deep concern regarding the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the grave prospect of an offensive in Rafah, and we support Council action to address this crisis. To build the broadest possible Council unity and facilitate real progress on the ground, the text should explicitly condemn Hamas's terror attacks and recognize the vital ongoing diplomatic negotiations to free the hostages and suspend hostilities.
messages.Malta: Malta expresses its gratitude to Algeria for presenting this essential draft resolution and firmly supports its call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, which remains the only realistic way to alleviate the catastrophic suffering in Gaza. We strongly endorse the demands for the immediate, unconditional release of all hostages and the full implementation of resolutions 2712 (2023) and 2720 (2023). Our minor suggested adjustments aim to further reinforce the protection of children and fundamental principles of international humanitarian law, and we stand ready to support the adoption of this text.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique fully supports the draft resolution presented by Algeria, which addresses the critical imperative of an immediate humanitarian ceasefire to halt the catastrophic loss of civilian life in Gaza. As an A3+ colleague, we commend Algeria's leadership and echo the deep concern over any impending ground offensive in Rafah, the urgent need for scaled-up humanitarian aid, and the immediate release of all hostages. The Council has a moral and legal duty to act without delay to protect civilians and uphold international humanitarian law.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea shares the deep concern regarding the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the imminent danger to civilians in Rafah, and we support the Council taking urgent action. However, to ensure broad consensus and moral clarity, the text should explicitly condemn the heinous 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas and underline that the release of all hostages is integral to achieving a sustainable cessation of hostilities. We stand ready to engage constructively to help achieve an actionable and unified Council outcome.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation fully supports the draft resolution submitted by Algeria and commends our Algerian colleagues for their principled initiative. An immediate humanitarian ceasefire is the Council's most urgent moral and political imperative to stop the ongoing carnage and avert an even greater catastrophe in Rafah. We insist that the draft not be diluted by endless negotiations or held hostage to Washington's diplomatic maneuvers, and we urge that it be put to a vote without delay.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone fully supports the draft resolution circulated by Algeria, which addresses the dire and deteriorating humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. The demand for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the protection of civilians, compliance with international law and the ICJ provisional measures, and the unconditional release of all hostages are indispensable priorities. We stand in full solidarity with our fellow African member state Algeria and urge the Council to adopt this text without delay.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia expresses its strong support for this draft resolution and thanks Algeria for bringing forward an essential call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. In light of the imminent catastrophic threat of an offensive on Rafah and the dire humanitarian catastrophe across Gaza, the Security Council must act decisively. We encourage maintaining firm language on international humanitarian law, the binding nature of the ICJ's provisional measures, and the immediate, unconditional release of all hostages.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland deeply appreciates Algeria's initiative and fully shares the grave concern regarding the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, the looming famine, and the disastrous consequences of a military offensive in Rafah. As depositary of the Geneva Conventions, Switzerland places the utmost importance on strict adherence to international humanitarian law by all parties, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. We believe the text would be strengthened by explicitly condemning the terror attacks of 7 October while maintaining a clear and urgent call for the protection of civilians.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom remains deeply alarmed by the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and the threat of an offensive into Rafah, but a Council resolution must reflect reality on the ground. Simply calling for an immediate ceasefire without addressing the fact that Hamas still holds hostages and retains the capacity to repeat the atrocities of 7 October will not bring lasting peace. We urge the penholder to explicitly condemn Hamas's terror attacks and focus the text on an immediate pause to get aid in and hostages out, leading towards a sustainable ceasefire.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support a draft resolution that demands an immediate, unconditional ceasefire, which would leave Hamas in power with the ability to repeat the horrors of October 7 and would undermine the delicate, high-stakes negotiations currently underway with Egypt and Qatar to secure the release of hostages. Any Council action must directly link a temporary cessation of hostilities to the release of all hostages and unequivocally condemn Hamas's terrorist atrocities. We urge the penholder to reconsider pressing this draft forward at this critical juncture.

steps.summary: Algeria has incorporated constructive amendments from Malta, Slovenia, Switzerland, Japan, and Ecuador that reinforce international humanitarian law, child protection, medical neutrality, ICRC access, and the binding ICJ provisional measures. However, Algeria firmly upholds the core mandate of the Arab Group, OIC, and the broader international community by demanding an immediate, unconditional humanitarian ceasefire in OP1 and rejecting attempts to dilute this demand or eliminate reference to the ICJ Order. The revised text preserves strong Council majority backing while remaining true to the urgent imperative to stop the bloodshed in Gaza.

messages.Ecuador: Ecuador welcomes the penholder's constructive engagement and the strengthening of OP4 regarding immediate and unconditional humanitarian access to all hostages, including by the ICRC. We reiterate our belief that an explicit condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks committed by Hamas would provide vital balance to the text. Nevertheless, given the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the urgent need to prevent further civilian suffering, Ecuador supports the draft resolution and the demand for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire.
messages.France: France reiterates its call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, and urgent humanitarian relief, especially facing the catastrophic risk of a military operation in Rafah. While we will vote in favour of this text given the acute humanitarian emergency on the ground, we continue to urge the penholder to explicitly condemn the terrorist attacks committed by Hamas and other groups on 7 October. Incorporating this language is essential for moral clarity and Council unity.
messages.Guyana: Guyana reaffirms its full and unreserved support for the draft resolution submitted by Algeria. An immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, and the unhindered flow of life-saving aid are imperative to prevent further catastrophic loss of civilian life, particularly in light of the looming offensive in Rafah. We thank the penholder for its leadership and stand ready to vote in favor of the text as presented.
messages.Japan: Japan appreciates the inclusion of PP8 taking note of the ongoing diplomatic efforts, as sensitive negotiations remain crucial to securing the release of hostages and alleviating civilian suffering. However, we continue to strongly urge the inclusion of an unequivocal condemnation of the terror attacks committed by Hamas on 7 October, which is vital for the Council's balanced and principled stance. Japan intends to support the draft given the catastrophic humanitarian crisis, but hopes these important elements can be accommodated to strengthen Council unity.
messages.Malta: Malta thanks Algeria for constructively accommodating our proposals in the revised draft, particularly regarding the disproportionate impact of the conflict on children and explicit adherence to the core international humanitarian law principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution. We believe the draft strikes the necessary balance by demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, and the unhindered flow of life-saving humanitarian assistance. Malta fully supports the draft resolution and stands ready to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique reiterates its full and unwavering support for the draft resolution put forward by our fellow A3+ member, Algeria. Given the catastrophic humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Gaza and the imminent threat facing Rafah, the Council must urgently act to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the protection of civilians, and the release of all hostages. We stand ready to vote in favour of this essential text as currently drafted.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea remains gravely concerned by the deepening humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and supports the urgent call for a humanitarian ceasefire and the protection of civilians. However, we continue to believe the Council's text would be significantly stronger and more balanced if it explicitly condemned the 7 October Hamas terrorist attacks and clearly linked the cessation of hostilities to the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We urge the penholder to consider these crucial elements as we finalize the draft.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation fully supports the draft resolution circulated by Algeria, which contains the long-overdue, unambiguous demand for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. We reject any further attempts by the United States to dilute the text, stall negotiations, or substitute Council action with vague promises of bilateral diplomacy. We urge the penholder to proceed to an immediate vote on the draft as currently formulated.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone reiterates its full and unwavering support for the draft resolution circulated by Algeria on behalf of our shared commitment to peace and humanitarian principles. The text is balanced, timely, and urgently needed to halt the catastrophic humanitarian crisis in Gaza and protect civilian lives. We stand ready to vote in favor of this resolution as drafted.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks Algeria for accommodating our proposed language regarding the binding nature of the International Court of Justice provisional measures and the explicit protection of humanitarian and medical personnel. The current text strikes a necessary and urgent balance, addressing the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, and securing the unconditional release of hostages. Slovenia fully supports the draft resolution as presented and is prepared to vote in favor.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland thanks Algeria for incorporating our proposal regarding the Geneva Conventions and their Additional Protocols into the preambular text. In light of the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the acute risk of famine, Switzerland supports the call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the release of hostages, and full respect for international humanitarian law. We nevertheless reiterate the importance of an explicit condemnation of the terrorist attacks committed by Hamas and other groups on 7 October 2023 to ensure a balanced and robust Council text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support a draft resolution that fails to condemn Hamas's heinous terrorist attacks of 7 October or call for a pathway to a sustainable ceasefire that ensures Hamas can never threaten Israel again. Simply calling for an immediate ceasefire without addressing the underlying conditions, including the release of all hostages and Hamas's continued control of Gaza, will not lead to durable peace. Unless these critical elements are addressed, the United Kingdom will be unable to vote in favour of the text and will abstain.
messages.United States of America: Proceeding to a vote on a draft demanding an unconditional immediate ceasefire will actively undermine sensitive, high-stakes negotiations currently underway between Egypt, Qatar, the United States, and Israel to secure the release of all hostages and establish an extended pause in fighting. A text that fails to condemn Hamas's terror attacks of October 7 and does not link a cessation of hostilities to the immediate release of hostages cannot achieve a durable peace. If this text is pressed to a vote in its current form, the United States will vote against it.

steps.summary: Algeria, on behalf of the Arab Group and in line with its principled defense of the Palestinian people, maintains the draft text calling for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, full respect for international law, and adherence to the binding ICJ provisional measures. Diluting the ceasefire demand or introducing selective condemnations would betray the urgent mandate to halt the slaughter in Gaza and prevent a catastrophic ground invasion of Rafah. The draft is pressed to a vote with overwhelming Council support of 13 members in favour.

before.Algeria:
Mr. President, 

Today, the Security Council is called upon to act in accordance with its primary responsibility under the Charter of the United Nations: the maintenance of international peace and security.

Algeria has put forward this draft resolution on behalf of the Arab Group and in response to the desperate appeals of millions of Palestinians and people of conscience across the world. The catastrophic situation in the Gaza Strip can no longer be tolerated. More than four months of relentless bombardment have claimed the lives of tens of thousands of innocent civilians, predominantly women and children, and brought the entire population of Gaza to the brink of famine. The prospect of an all-out military offensive on Rafah, where nearly 1.5 million displaced people are crowded into dire conditions with nowhere left to flee, threatens an even greater catastrophe.

Our draft resolution is clear, balanced, and vital. It demands an immediate humanitarian ceasefire that must be respected by all parties. It demands the unconditional release of all hostages. It calls for unhindered humanitarian assistance at scale throughout the entire Gaza Strip. It unequivocally rejects the forced displacement of the Palestinian people and takes note of the binding provisional measures indicated by the International Court of Justice.

Silence and inaction are not an option. A vote in favour of this text is a vote in support of the Palestinian people’s right to life. Conversely, voting against it endorses the brutal violence and collective punishment inflicted upon them. Each member of this Council must choose where it stands. We urge all Council members to shoulder their moral and legal responsibilities and vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.United States of America:
Colleagues, over the past several months, the United States has been actively engaged in intensive diplomacy on the ground with partners in the region—specifically Egypt and Qatar—to secure a deal that would see the release of hostages and create an extended humanitarian pause in fighting, longer than anything we have seen to date. 

Demanding an immediate, unconditional ceasefire without requiring Hamas to release the hostages will not bring about a durable peace. Instead, it could extend the fighting between Hamas and Israel, keep hostages in captivity, and exacerbate the dire humanitarian crisis facing Palestinians in Gaza. Proceeding with a vote today on this draft resolution is irresponsible and risks jeopardizing the sensitive, ongoing negotiations that offer the best viable path toward a cessation of hostilities and getting life-saving aid to those who need it most. 

Furthermore, this text fails to condemn Hamas’s horrific terrorist attacks of October 7, an omission this Council cannot continue to ignore. For these reasons, while we understand the desire of many Council members to see urgent action, the United States cannot support a draft resolution that undermines critical diplomatic efforts on the ground. We will vote against it.

after.China:
China voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Algeria on behalf of the Arab Group. We express our strong disappointment and dissatisfaction with the outcome of the vote.

The draft resolution put forward by Algeria was based on the minimum requirements of humanity and the urgent call of the international community. It demanded an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the release of all hostages, the guaranteed delivery of humanitarian assistance, and the rejection of forced displacement. These provisions are not only urgently needed to save lives in Gaza, but also represent the broad consensus of the members of the Council and the overwhelming majority of the United Nations membership. 

The use of the veto by the United States to block this draft resolution sends entirely the wrong message, pushing the situation in Gaza into an even more dangerous direction. Given the current situation, continued passive avoidance of an immediate ceasefire is nothing different from giving a green light to the continued slaughter of civilians. 

The claim that a Council resolution demanding a ceasefire would disrupt ongoing diplomatic negotiations is totally untenable. Over the past four months of conflict, tens of thousands of innocent civilians, predominantly women and children, have lost their lives, and over a million people have been displaced. A ceasefire is not an obstacle to negotiations; rather, it is the fundamental prerequisite to save lives, to create the conditions for diplomatic efforts, and to prevent the conflict from spiralling further out of control. 

At present, the situation in Rafah is perilous in the extreme. More than 1.4 million Palestinians are trapped with nowhere else to go. An Israeli military ground offensive against Rafah would cause an unimaginable humanitarian catastrophe and must be unequivocally opposed. The Council must uphold international law, including international humanitarian law, and respect the provisional measures indicated by the International Court of Justice. 

The spillover effects of the Gaza conflict are already destabilizing the wider Middle East, increasing the risk of a regional war. The Security Council must shoulder its primary responsibility under the Charter for the maintenance of international peace and security. Although the draft resolution was vetoed, the strong call of the international community for a ceasefire, an end to the fighting, and the protection of civilians will not subside. 

China will continue to work tirelessly with the international community to bring about an immediate cessation of hostilities, to alleviate the humanitarian catastrophe, and to advance a comprehensive, just, and lasting settlement of the question of Palestine based on the two-State solution.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Algeria. We regret that, once again, the Security Council has been unable to adopt a text in the face of the ongoing tragedy in Gaza.

The humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip is catastrophic. The human toll is intolerable, and the risk of famine is imminent. France recalls that there is an absolute urgency to conclude, without further delay, an agreement on a ceasefire that finally guarantees the protection of all civilians and the massive, unhindered entry of emergency aid. 

This is why France has consistently called for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire that must lead to a permanent ceasefire. 

France reiterates its firm opposition to an Israeli ground offensive in Rafah, which would lead to an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe and could lead to forced displacement of populations, which would constitute a severe violation of international humanitarian law.

At the same time, we must not lose sight of the origins of this tragedy. France condemns in the strongest terms the horrific terrorist attacks committed by Hamas and other terrorist groups on 7 October. We reiterate our demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages still held in Gaza, and we call for immediate humanitarian access to them. It is incomprehensible that this Council has still not been able to explicitly condemn these terrorist acts.

International humanitarian law applies to everyone and must be respected by all in all circumstances. The fight against terrorism cannot serve as a justification for failing to comply with international humanitarian law. Israel must facilitate the entry of humanitarian aid into and throughout the Gaza Strip and ensure that all crossing points are opened, including the Kerem Shalom crossing and the port of Ashdod.

Finally, we must also address the situation in the West Bank and East Jerusalem, where the escalation of settler violence is unacceptable. France has recently adopted sanctions against violent extremist Israeli settlers and will continue to act firmly in this regard.

Only a political solution based on the two-State solution—with two democratic States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security, with Jerusalem as the capital of both States—can bring lasting peace to Israelis and Palestinians alike. France will continue its tireless mobilization to this end, in close coordination with all our regional and international partners.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Guyana:
Mr. President,

Guyana voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Algeria on behalf of the Arab Group, and we deeply regret that, once again, the Security Council has been prevented from demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire in Gaza.

More than four months of relentless military operations have devastated the Gaza Strip. Over 29,000 Palestinians, the vast majority of them women and children, have been killed. Countless more lie buried under the rubble. More than 80 per cent of the population has been forcibly displaced, and widespread starvation and disease now threaten the lives of hundreds of thousands of civilians. Human suffering has reached unimaginable proportions.

Guyana is especially alarmed by the prospect of an expanded ground offensive into Rafah, where nearly 1.5 million Palestinians—having fled bombardment across northern and central Gaza—are sheltering in extremely dire, overcrowded, and life-threatening conditions. A military operation in Rafah would be catastrophic and would inevitably result in mass civilian casualties and the further collapse of the already decimated humanitarian response. As the Secretary-General and humanitarian agencies have warned, there is nowhere safe left to go in Gaza.

The draft resolution before us today captured the most essential priorities: demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, demanding compliance by all parties with their obligations under international humanitarian law, rejecting the forced displacement of civilians, demanding the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid at scale, and demanding the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. It also appropriately took note of the binding provisional measures indicated by the International Court of Justice on 26 January.

None of these demands should be controversial. They reflect basic obligations under international law and the Charter of the United Nations. Council action demanding an immediate ceasefire cannot continue to be indefinitely deferred while tens of thousands of innocent lives are extinguished and the region teeters on the brink of wider conflict.

Guyana reiterates its condemnation of all attacks against civilians and civilian objects, as well as all acts of terrorism. We reiterate our urgent call for the immediate, unconditional release of all hostages and for their humane treatment.

Mr. President,

Military operations will not bring enduring peace or security to either Israelis or Palestinians. The only viable path forward is an immediate ceasefire, accompanied by unhindered humanitarian access and meaningful political dialogue toward a just and comprehensive peace based on the two-State solution, where Israel and Palestine live side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders.

Guyana will continue to support all efforts directed at ending the suffering of the Palestinian people and restoring the credibility and authority of this Council.

I thank you.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Algeria.

The humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip is catastrophic. More than four months into the conflict, the loss of innocent civilian lives, the majority of them women and children, continues to mount. Famine is looming, and access to essential supplies, including food, water, and medical care, remains severely constrained. Furthermore, we are deeply concerned by reports of a possible military operation in Rafah, where over a million displaced Palestinians have sought refuge in precarious conditions. A humanitarian ceasefire must be realized immediately to ensure a conducive environment for delivering life-saving humanitarian assistance at scale, to secure the release of all hostages, and to pave the way toward a sustainable cessation of hostilities.

At the same time, Japan reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of the terror attacks committed by Hamas and others on 7 October, and we demand once again the immediate and unconditional release of all remaining hostages. 

We also recognize and highly appreciate the tireless and sensitive diplomatic negotiations being pursued on the ground by the United States, Egypt, and Qatar to secure an agreement that would release hostages and achieve an extended humanitarian pause. These diplomatic efforts are vital to making tangible improvements on the ground.

Japan deeply regrets that the Council was unable to speak with one voice today. Nevertheless, the Security Council must not abandon its responsibility. We urge all parties to strictly comply with international humanitarian law and to fully implement resolutions 2712 (2023) and 2720 (2023). Japan remains committed to working actively with Council members and regional partners to alleviate the humanitarian suffering and to revitalize the political process towards a two-State solution, where both Israelis and Palestinians can live side by side in peace and security.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Malta:
Mr. President,

Malta voted in favour of the draft resolution presented by Algeria, and we deeply regret that, once again, the Security Council was unable to adopt a resolution demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire.

For over four months, the civilian population in Gaza has been subjected to unimaginable suffering, death, and destruction. More than 28,000 Palestinians have been killed, the overwhelming majority of them women and children. The healthcare system has been brought to the point of collapse, as evidenced by the devastating situation at Nasser and Al-Amal hospitals. The entire population is now facing the acute and imminent risk of famine. 

Malta is gravely alarmed by the prospect of an Israeli military ground offensive into Rafah, where nearly 1.5 million displaced persons are sheltering in desperate, overcrowded, and squalid conditions. There is nowhere left for them to go, and nowhere in Gaza is safe. Such an operation would have catastrophic consequences for civilians and must not take place.

An immediate humanitarian ceasefire is urgently required. It is the only tangible way to halt the carnage, prevent further civilian casualties, and ensure that life-saving humanitarian assistance can be delivered safely, rapidly, and at scale throughout the entire Gaza Strip.

At the same time, Malta reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of the horrific terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas and other armed groups on 7 October. We reiterate our demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, as well as immediate humanitarian access to address their medical needs.

All parties must strictly adhere to their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution must be respected at all times. Civilians, hospitals, medical workers, and humanitarian personnel must be protected. We also recall the binding nature of the provisional measures ordered by the International Court of Justice on 26 January.

We call for the full, immediate, and unhindered implementation of Council resolutions 2712 (2023) and 2720 (2023). 

Finally, Malta reaffirms its unwavering commitment to a two-State solution, in line with relevant United Nations resolutions, with the Gaza Strip constituting an integral part of a sovereign, viable, and independent Palestinian State living side by side with Israel in peace and security.

The Council cannot remain paralyzed while innocent lives continue to be lost every day. We must live up to our Charter responsibilities.

Thank you.
after.Republic of Korea:
Mr. President,

The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Algeria today.

Our vote reflects our deep and pressing concern over the catastrophic humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip. More than four months into the conflict, the human toll has been devastating, with civilian casualties continuing to climb, disproportionately affecting women and children. The acute shortage of food, water, and medical supplies has brought the civilian population to the brink of famine, while health facilities have collapsed. Moreover, we share the grave concern expressed by many regarding the prospect of an expanded military ground operation in Rafah, where more than a million displaced Palestinians are sheltering in extremely vulnerable conditions with nowhere safe to go. In this light, an immediate humanitarian ceasefire is urgently required to save lives and enable the delivery of humanitarian assistance at scale.

At the same time, my delegation emphasizes that this crisis was sparked by the brutal terrorist attacks committed by Hamas against Israel on 7 October. We reiterate our unequivocal condemnation of those acts of terrorism. The immediate and unconditional release of all hostages remaining in captivity, along with immediate humanitarian access to meet their medical needs, must be fulfilled without delay.

The Republic of Korea also fully recognizes and appreciates the tireless diplomatic efforts being pursued on the ground by the United States, Qatar, and Egypt to secure an agreement on the release of hostages and an extended humanitarian pause. Such diplomatic negotiations are vital, and we sincerely hope they will yield tangible results soon.

Ultimately, lasting peace and security cannot be achieved through arms. We reiterate our unwavering commitment to the two-State solution, where Israel and Palestine live side by side in peace and security within recognized borders, as the only viable and just path forward.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

Today we have witnessed another black page in the history of the Security Council, written once again by the delegation of the United States of America. 

Washington has once again used its veto to block the Security Council from fulfilling its primary responsibility under the United Nations Charter: to maintain international peace and security and to halt the bloodshed in the Gaza Strip. By voting against the draft resolution submitted by Algeria on behalf of the Arab Group, which was supported by 13 members of the Council, the United States has once again shown its true face and demonstrated utter disregard for the will of the overwhelming majority of the international community.

For months, the American delegation has been trying to convince the Council and world public opinion that quiet diplomacy is underway, that sensitive negotiations on the ground require silence, and that any action by the Security Council would somehow disrupt them. Today’s veto has definitively exposed this narrative for what it is: a cynical smoke screen designed to buy time for Israel to complete its brutal military operation and collective punishment of the Palestinian civilian population, including through the announced and catastrophic assault on Rafah, where nearly one and a half million Palestinians are trapped with nowhere left to flee.

Washington is not interested in peace or in saving civilian lives. Instead, it continues to provide an unconditional diplomatic shield and an open-ended license to kill. The United States bears full responsibility for the consequences of today's decision, which leaves the civilian population of Gaza at the mercy of bombardment, disease, and starvation.

The draft resolution presented by our Algerian colleagues was balanced, urgent, and strictly humanitarian. It demanded an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the release of hostages, and full humanitarian access. Algeria conducted extensive consultations in good faith and made numerous compromises. Yet, no compromise was ever going to satisfy Washington, whose only objective has been to prevent the Security Council from calling things by their proper names and demanding an immediate halt to hostilities.

The alternative draft that the United States is hastily attempting to introduce is nothing more than another attempt to pull wool over the eyes of the international community, provide cover for the continuation of military action, and impose Washington's own self-serving geopolitical agenda on the region.

The Russian Federation will continue to stand firmly with the Palestinian people and the Arab group, and we will not cease our efforts to achieve an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire in Gaza, which is the only viable path to saving lives and creating conditions for a comprehensive, just, and lasting settlement on the universally recognized international legal basis of the two-State solution.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

Sierra Leone voted in favour of the draft resolution contained in document S/2024/173, submitted by Algeria on behalf of the Arab Group, and we express our deep regret that the Security Council has once again failed to adopt a resolution demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire in Gaza.

The situation on the ground in the Gaza Strip is catastrophic, untenable, and intolerable. Over four months of relentless hostilities have resulted in the tragic loss of tens of thousands of civilian lives, predominantly women and children. Infrastructure has been decimated, the health system has collapsed, and the acute risk of famine now looms large over the civilian population. A potential military ground operation in Rafah, where more than 1.4 million internally displaced persons are trapped in extremely precarious and life-threatening conditions, would only exacerbate this human tragedy and have catastrophic consequences that this Council cannot ignore.

It was against this harrowing backdrop that Sierra Leone supported the draft resolution. The draft text before us was balanced, urgent, and necessary. It demanded an immediate humanitarian ceasefire to end the bloodshed, create conducive conditions for the delivery of humanitarian assistance at scale, and protect civilian lives. It also explicitly demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, condemned all acts of terrorism and violence against civilians, and unequivocally rejected the forced displacement of the Palestinian population in violation of international law.

Furthermore, we recall the binding Order of the International Court of Justice of 26 January 2024 on provisional measures, which all parties are obligated to comply with, as well as full compliance with international humanitarian law and international human rights law.

Mr. President,

The Security Council has a primary responsibility under the Charter of the United Nations for the maintenance of international peace and security. Our failure to act today diminishes our credibility and deepens the suffering of innocent civilians who look to this Council for hope and protection. 

Sierra Leone reaffirms its firm conviction that a military approach cannot bring durable peace, security, or stability to the region. The only viable path to ending this protracted conflict remains the two-State solution, where Israel and Palestine live side by side in peace, security, and dignity, within secure and recognized borders based on the 1967 lines. 

We urge the Council and all relevant actors to redouble their diplomatic efforts to bring an immediate halt to the hostilities, secure the release of all hostages, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and restore a credible political horizon towards sustainable peace.

I thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Mr. President,

Slovenia voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Algeria, and we deeply regret that the Council was once again unable to unite and speak with one voice in the face of the catastrophic humanitarian tragedy unfolding in Gaza.

For more than four months, civilians in Gaza have been enduring unimaginable suffering. Tens of thousands of people, predominantly women and children, have lost their lives, and the humanitarian situation has reached unprecedented and catastrophic levels, with an imminent risk of famine and a near-total collapse of the healthcare system. 

The draft resolution before us today reflected the bare minimum of what this Council should demand: an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, full and unhindered humanitarian access at scale, and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure in accordance with international humanitarian law. 

We are particularly alarmed by the prospect of a full-scale ground offensive in Rafah, where nearly 1.5 million displaced Palestinians are sheltering under desperate and life-threatening conditions, with nowhere safe left to go. Such an operation would have catastrophic consequences and must not happen.

Slovenia reiterates that all parties must scrupulously comply with international law, including international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The provisional measures ordered by the International Court of Justice are binding and must be implemented. We also reiterate our firm rejection of any forced displacement of the Palestinian population.

While we support all ongoing diplomatic efforts by the United States, Qatar, and Egypt to secure an agreement for the release of hostages and an extended pause in hostilities, this cannot relieve the Security Council of its Charter-mandated responsibility to act to protect civilians and maintain international peace and security.

Finally, we reiterate our steadfast commitment to a two-State solution, where Israel and Palestine live side by side in peace and security, as the only viable foundation for lasting peace in the region. Slovenia will continue to engage constructively with all Council members to achieve these vital objectives.

I thank you.
after.Switzerland:
Mr. President,

Switzerland voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Algeria, and we deeply regret that the Council was once again unable to adopt it.

More than four months into this conflict, the humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip is catastrophic. Tens of thousands of civilians, the majority of them women and children, have lost their lives. Famine is looming, access to basic necessities and medical care is almost non-existent, and disease is spreading rapidly. The prospect of a large-scale military offensive on Rafah, where nearly 1.5 million displaced people are crowded in appalling and precarious conditions with nowhere left to go, is of the utmost concern. Such an offensive would have devastating consequences for civilians and must not take place.

It is for these reasons that Switzerland supported the call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. An immediate cessation of hostilities is urgently needed to allow life-saving humanitarian assistance to reach all civilians in need safely, rapidly, and without hindrance, and to secure the release of all hostages. 

As depositary of the Geneva Conventions, Switzerland reminds all parties of their strict obligation to respect and ensure respect for international humanitarian law in all circumstances. Civilians and civilian objects, including hospitals, medical and humanitarian personnel, and United Nations facilities, must be protected. The principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution must be observed. 

Switzerland reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of the horrific terrorist acts committed by Hamas and other armed groups on 7 October 2023, as well as the indiscriminate firing of rockets into Israel. We demand once again the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and that the International Committee of the Red Cross be granted immediate access to them. While recognizing Israel’s legitimate right to ensure its security and defence, this right must be exercised strictly within the framework of international law, in particular international humanitarian law.

We also reject any forced displacement of the civilian population, which constitutes a violation of international humanitarian law.

Finally, we must look beyond the immediate crisis. A durable cessation of hostilities must pave the way toward a political horizon. Switzerland remains firmly convinced that the only viable path to sustainable peace and security for both Israelis and Palestinians is a negotiated two-State solution, where two democratic States, Israel and Palestine, live side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders. 

Switzerland will continue to work tirelessly with all Council members and partners in the region to achieve these vital objectives.

Thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom abstained on the draft resolution before us today because of our concern that calling for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire—as this text does—without conditions being met will not bring about a durable peace.

Simply calling for an immediate ceasefire will not make it happen. And a ceasefire that allows Hamas to regroup and retain the capability to launch further attacks on Israel, or one that leaves hostages in captivity, will not lead to the sustainable peace that both Israelis and Palestinians so desperately need.

Our goal must be not simply an end to fighting today, but a durable, permanent peace. As the Foreign Secretary has set out, the best way to achieve this is through an immediate humanitarian pause to get aid in and hostages out, which can then be turned into a sustainable, permanent ceasefire without a return to destruction, fighting, and loss of life.

For a ceasefire to last, several conditions must be met: all hostages must be released; the capacity of Hamas to launch further attacks against Israel must be removed; Hamas must no longer be in charge of Gaza; and there must be a credible political horizon towards a two-State solution, with a reformed Palestinian Authority supported by an international package.

At the same time, we remain deeply alarmed by the prospect of an Israeli military offensive into Rafah, where over a million displaced civilians are sheltering. An offensive there would have catastrophic consequences for civilians who have nowhere else to go. We urge Israel not to proceed with a military operation in Rafah.

The humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic. Palestinians are facing acute shortages of food, clean water, and medical care, and the risk of famine is imminent. We reiterate our call for Israel to allow full, rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access at scale, to open more border crossings, including Kerem Shalom and Ashdod port, and to ensure the protection of aid workers and medical personnel in full accordance with international humanitarian law. 

We will continue to work tirelessly with our partners in the region and across the Security Council to secure an immediate pause in fighting, the release of all hostages, a massive increase in humanitarian aid, and progress towards a sustainable, permanent peace.
